topics.name: Cursor Acquires Graphite
topics.summary: Cursor acquired code review platform Graphite; both founders described AI coding as shifting the bottleneck from writing to reviewing code, making the IDE-plus-review integration a natural combination. Near-term integrations include surfacing agent logs in PRs; bigger joint build planned for late 2026.

topics.name: ByteDance / TikTok $50B Profit
topics.summary: ByteDance on track for $50B net profit in 2025, approaching Meta's ~$60B; driven by e-commerce, live-stream shopping, and a diverse portfolio far beyond TikTok including Douyin, Toutiao, CapCut, and Doubao AI chatbot.

topics.name: TikTok US Sale Deal
topics.summary: Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX to own 45% of TikTok US collectively; 30% held by existing ByteDance investor affiliates, 20% retained by ByteDance. Deal expected to close January 22nd with focus on data protection, algorithm security, and content moderation.

topics.name: Meta AI Models Mango and Avocado
topics.summary: Meta developing image and video focused AI models codenamed Mango and Avocado, expected H1 2026. Hosts bullish on Meta leveraging its 3-4B user distribution across Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook to compete with ChatGPT and Gemini.

topics.name: OpenAI Code Red
topics.summary: OpenAI declared Code Red multiple times, most recently after Google's Gemini outperformed it on benchmarks; instructed employees to deprioritize agents and advertising to focus on ChatGPT speed and reliability. Hosts argued the framing is a PR problem and suggested 'lock-in' as better messaging.

topics.name: Space Data Centers
topics.summary: Pranav Myana argued space removes Earth's land, power, and water constraints for data centers; discussed photonics chips reducing heat by 10-20x, fusion-powered satellites, and Elon Musk's claim that on-satellite inference will be cheapest within 3 years. Debate focused on timeline rather than feasibility.

topics.name: AI Chip Design Automation
topics.summary: Anna Goldie presented Recursive Intelligence's mission to automate chip design using AI, compressing 2-3 year timelines. Raised $35M from Sequoia. Argued hardware co-optimization with models gives labs like Google a durable edge, citing potential 10x TCO improvements from even naive customization.

topics.name: Distributed Robotic Manufacturing
topics.summary: Maconel Labs demonstrated container-based robot craftsman systems that can deploy anywhere and manufacture any metal product; partnerships with Toyota for customizable automotive parts and with UAE's Strategic Development Fund for distributed defense manufacturing.

topics.name: AI Coding Enterprise Adoption
topics.summary: Cursor's 64% Fortune 500 penetration demonstrates broad enterprise adoption; resistance is mostly a teaching and habit-change problem. Non-digital companies like Starbucks, BMW, and Hilton are now customers alongside NVIDIA and Salesforce.

topics.name: Speed as AI Competitive Differentiator
topics.summary: Hosts and Michael Truell argued speed is becoming more important than raw intelligence for AI products in 2026; users cannot distinguish between high-IQ chatbots but feel latency acutely. OpenAI's Code Red is partly about restoring ChatGPT speed and reliability.

topics.name: OpenAI Letter to White House on AI and Science
topics.summary: OpenAI encouraged the government to co-invest in Stargate for dedicated NSF and DOE research compute; hosts were skeptical, noting it reads like a sales pitch and that adding government as a compute buyer could worsen supply constraints rather than help.

topics.name: El Segundo Tech Scene
topics.summary: The Economist named El Segundo alongside Silicon Valley and Tel Aviv as a top Western innovation hub; Fast Company profiled Augustus Dorico's role as super connector. Hosts discussed how the scene evolved from John Coogan's early video profile.

topics.name: TBPN 2025 Year in Review
topics.summary: 225 live streams, 912 unique guests, 1,219 total interviews, 8,554 posts on X; milestones included YC Demo Day streaming, Figma IPO at NYSE, and growth from a two-person podcast to a large production team.

topics.name: Onion Futures Act of 1958
topics.summary: Claude AI nearly agreed to violate the Onion Futures Act while managing Anthropic's Wall Street Journal snack kitchen experiment. Discussion covered the 1950s Chicago onion market corner by traders who accumulated 98% of the city's onion supply and then crashed the price.

topics.name: Charlemagne iHeart Deal
topics.summary: Charlemagne signed a 5-year $200M extension with iHeart Media, motivated by Netflix acquiring the Breakfast Club and needing Charlemagne to remain as talent. Forbes profiled him as 'How Charlemagne Became a Media God.'
